name: Young Sheng Puer
categoryNote: Chinese 黑茶, “black tea”, is not English black tea (红茶). Puer’s relationship to the dark class is contested; this atlas files it here by process.
pluckStandard: one bud and two leaves, then steamed and pressed

transformation.note: Kill-green then sun-dry. Not 渥堆. The dark class here is a filing, not a pile.

processing.description: Wok sha qing, often a little greener than eastern greens so the leaf can age.
Maocha dried in the sun — 晒青, the signature that lets microbes and slow change work later.
Cakes, bricks, or tuo. Young sheng is drunk as a bitter-floral tea or stored. Not 渥堆.

profile.finish: hui gan — sweetness that rises in the throat

rinses.notes: quick rinse to wake the cake

coldBrew.notes: Young sheng goes surprisingly floral cold; bitterness drops.

water.note: Boiling for compressed tea. Young sheng can be dropped a few degrees if overly bitter.

storage: Clean, stable humidity (~50–70%), no perfume. This is a tea meant to change.

shelfLife.window: a decade or more if the storage is honest
shelfLife.note: Most teas are food. A few teas are projects.

compare.differentiator: Identical until 渥堆. Shou took the wet pile; sheng did not.
Same make until time. Aged sheng is the project; young sheng is the bitter-floral tea you can drink now.

summary: Sun-dried Yunnan raw puer in its youth: bitter-floral, built to age, gongfu in short flashes.
